features.summary: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.
Your Speed increases while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, as shown on the Monk Features table.
Unarmed Strikes may use Strength or Dexterity, and your Martial Arts die replaces their base damage.

When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack's total damage by 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your Monk level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect it: a creature you can see within 5 feet (melee attack) or 60 feet (ranged attack) and not behind Total Cover makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Focus save DC, taking two Martial Arts dice plus your Dexterity modifier damage of the attack's type on a failure.
Your Deflect Attacks works against attacks that deal any damage type, not only Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing.

Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain benefits: Flurry makes three Unarmed Strikes, a paid Patient Defense grants Temporary Hit Points equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die, and a paid Step of the Wind can carry a willing Large or smaller creature within 5 feet with you.
When you take a Bonus Action other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind immediately after that Bonus Action.
You gain Focus Points that fuel Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind.

When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points and roll your Martial Arts die, regaining Hit Points equal to your Monk level plus the roll. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Spend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action.
Take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action, or spend 1 Focus Point to Disengage and Dodge together.
Take the Dash action as a Bonus Action, or spend 1 Focus Point to Dash and Disengage together.
When you roll Initiative and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.
You gain proficiency in all saving throws. In addition, when you fail a saving throw, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have Resistance to all damage except Force damage.

At the end of each of your turns, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself: Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned. In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn't give you levels of Exhaustion.

When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. You don't benefit from this feature while Incapacitated.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target makes a Constitution saving throw: on a failure it has the Stunned condition, on a success its Speed is halved and the next attack roll against it has Advantage, both until the start of your next turn.
Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

Whenever you hit a creature with an attack granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following on that target: Addle (no Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn), Push (Strength save or pushed up to 15 feet away), or Topple (Dexterity save or Prone).

As a Bonus Action, you can roll your Martial Arts die. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point regained). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 4 Focus Points to start imperceptible vibrations that last a number of days equal to your Monk level. You can end them harmlessly (no action required), or take an action to end them: the target then makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 Force damage on a failure or half as much on a success. You and the target must be on the same plane. You can have only one creature under this effect at a time.

You have a pool of healing power that replenishes on a Long Rest. As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature and restore a number of Hit Points from that pool, or expend 5 Hit Points from the pool to remove the Poisoned condition.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Divine Sense is a Bonus Action of this class.

When you use Lay On Hands, you can also remove one or more of these conditions from the target: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned. You expend 5 Hit Points from the pool for each condition removed.
When you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Devotion Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

When you take the Attack action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to imbue one Melee weapon you are holding: for 10 minutes you add your Charisma modifier (minimum +1) to attack rolls with it, each hit deals its normal damage type or Radiant, and it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light 20 feet beyond. The effect ends early if you are not carrying the weapon.
Divine Smite is always prepared; one free cast per Long Rest.
While not Incapacitated, you and allies within 10 feet gain a saving-throw bonus equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1); only one such aura benefits a creature at a time.
You and allies in your Aura of Protection have Immunity to Charmed; an existing Charmed condition has no effect while there.
You and your allies have Immunity to the Frightened condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Frightened ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.
Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot Emanation.

Magic action, one Channel Divinity: up to your Charisma modifier (minimum one) creatures you can see within 60 feet make a Wisdom save or are Frightened for 1 minute or until they take damage. While Frightened this way a creature can move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action on its turn -- only one of the three.
Whenever you cast Divine Smite, you and your allies have Half Cover while in your Aura of Protection. The benefit lasts until the start of your next turn.
When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

As a Bonus Action, you radiate a 30-foot Emanation for 10 minutes or until you end it (no action required). You have Advantage on saving throws forced by a Fiend or an Undead, an enemy that starts its turn in the aura takes Radiant damage equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus, and the aura is filled with Bright Light.
Bonus Action: regain HP equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level. You have two uses (three at Fighter level 4, four at level 10); regain one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long Rest.
Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
You can use the mastery properties of your weapons. (This slice approximates the chosen-weapons list with an 'equipped weapon' unlock; the count track is not yet consumed.)
On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on a turn.

When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of Second Wind to roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, rather than regaining Hit Points. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.
When you take the Attack action, you can attack twice instead of once. Extra Attack never stacks: a character that gains it from a second class uses the highest value, not the sum.
Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

You have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks. In addition, immediately after you score a Critical Hit, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
You gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.
During combat, you can give yourself Heroic Inspiration whenever you start your turn without it.
When you take the Attack action, you can attack three times instead of once.
Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can now score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.
You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, treat a roll of 18-20 on one as a 20, and while Bloodied you regain 5 plus your Constitution modifier Hit Points at the start of each of your turns.

When you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level, and you must use the new roll. You have two uses at level 13 and three at level 17, and you regain all uses on a Long Rest.
When you take the Attack action, you can attack four times instead of once.
If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1. In addition, while your Rage is active, whenever you make an ability check using Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability.
While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.
Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. A Shield does not interfere.
You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.
As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.
You have Advantage on Initiative rolls.

Bonus Action: enter a Rage. While raging, Strength attacks and Unarmed Strikes deal extra damage (see the Barbarian table), and your Strength saving throws have advantage. You cannot cast spells or maintain Concentration while raging; entering a Rage ends Concentration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn; making an attack against an enemy, or using a Bonus Action, extends it for another turn, up to 10 turns. It ends early if you are Incapacitated. You regain one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long Rest.
You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions while your Rage is active. If you are Charmed or Frightened when you enter your Rage, the condition ends on you.
When a creature within 5 feet of you deals damage to you, you can use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. On a success, your Hit Points change to twice your Barbarian level instead. Each use after the first raises the DC by 5; a Short or Long Rest resets it to 10.

When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage; once you do so, you can't do it again until you finish a Long Rest. Your Rage also lasts 10 minutes without needing to extend it from round to round, and it ends early only if you have the Unconscious condition or don Heavy armor.

When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

If you use Reckless Attack while your Rage is active, you deal extra damage to the first target you hit on your turn with a Strength-based attack. To determine the extra damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. The damage has the same type as the weapon or Unarmed Strike used for the attack.

If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have Disadvantage. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or Unarmed Strike, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice.

Staggering Blow: the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn. Sundering Blow: before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll.
If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

As a Bonus Action, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, it has the Frightened condition for 1 minute, and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore it.
You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in Character Creation.
Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in those skills. At Rogue level 6, choose two more.

Once per turn, when you hit with an attack using a Finesse or Ranged weapon, deal extra damage if you have Advantage, or if an ally who is not Incapacitated is within 5 feet of the target and you do not have Disadvantage. The damage type matches the weapon.

As a Bonus Action, you give yourself Advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your Speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.
You can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a Bonus Action.
You can use a Bonus Action to make a Sleight of Hand check or to take the Utilize action.
You gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed. You can also determine your jump distance using your Dexterity rather than your Strength.
When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (rounded down).

When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. You can't use this feature while Incapacitated.
Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

You can attune to up to four magic items at once. Whenever you use a magic item property that expends charges, roll 1d6; on a 6 the property works without expending charges. You can use any Spell Scroll, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability.
You can take two turns during the first round of any combat: your first turn at your normal Initiative and your second turn at your Initiative minus 10.
When you fail a D20 Test, you can turn the roll into a 20. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can spend Sneak Attack dice on one effect before rolling the damage: Poison, Trip, or Withdraw. A save against it uses DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity modifier.
You can use two Cunning Strike effects on the same Sneak Attack, paying the dice cost of each.
Daze, Knock Out, and Obscure join your Cunning Strike options.
Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in that skill.
Languages. You know two languages of your choice from the language tables in Character Creation. (The other half of Deft Explorer is declared separately because a feature carries one choice slot.)

You always have the Hunter's Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a Long Rest. The number of free casts increases at certain Ranger levels.
Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in those skills.

As a Magic action, you can give yourself Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Whenever you finish a Short Rest, your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1.
Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.
Your connection to the forces of nature grants you Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.
The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.
While a creature is marked by your Hunter's Mark, you know whether that creature has any Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.
You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.
When you hit a creature with a weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage to the target if it's missing any of its Hit Points. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target, that is within the weapon's range, and that you haven't attacked this turn.
You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.
Opportunity Attacks have Disadvantage against you.
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, that creature has Disadvantage on all other attack rolls against you this turn.

Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark, you can also deal that spell's extra damage to a different creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature.
When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to give yourself Resistance to that damage and any other damage of the same type until the end of the current turn.

As a Bonus Action, you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the die and add the number rolled to the d20. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.
You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.
Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in those skills. At Bard level 9, choose two more.
You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, use your Reaction and spend one Bardic Inspiration use to roll your Bardic Inspiration die and subtract it from the roll.

You learn two spells of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. A chosen spell must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots. You always have them prepared and they don't count against your Prepared Spells number; whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of them.

Whenever you reach a Bard level and the Prepared Spells number increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard lists; those spells count as Bard spells. Whenever you replace a prepared spell, it can come from those lists too. This never changes how many spells you can prepare.

When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. On a failure, the Bardic Inspiration isn't expended.
When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage.

You can expend a spell slot to gain Sorcery Points equal to its level (no action required), or spend Sorcery Points as a Bonus Action to create one temporary spell slot of level 1 to 5. A created slot vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.
Once per Long Rest, when you finish a Short Rest, regain expended Sorcery Points, up to a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down).
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Your Hit Point maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level. While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.

As a Bonus Action, you sprout dragon wings for 1 hour or until you dismiss them (no action required). For the duration you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you spend 3 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore it.
Bonus Action, 1 minute: your Sorcerer spell save DC increases by 1 and you have Advantage on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast. Twice per Long Rest.

You know two Metamagic options and can apply one to a spell you cast (two while Sorcery Incarnate is active). You gain two more at levels 10 and 17, and may replace one whenever you gain a Sorcerer level.
With no Innate Sorcery uses left, spend 2 Sorcery Points to activate it. While it is active you can apply up to two Metamagic options to each spell.
While Innate Sorcery is active you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.
When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fiend Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.
When you reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1).

After you make an ability check or a saving throw and see the result but before it takes effect, spend one use to add 1d10 to the roll; once per roll; uses equal to Charisma modifier (min 1); regain all on a long rest.
Choose one damage type other than Force whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest. You have Resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.
Once per Long Rest you can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots, up to half your maximum (round up).
You always have Contact Other Plane prepared. Once per Long Rest you can cast it without expending a spell slot, and you automatically succeed on that spell's saving throw.
Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and regain the use when you finish a Long Rest.
Choose one level 7 Warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and regain the use when you finish a Long Rest.
Choose one level 8 Warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and regain the use when you finish a Long Rest.
Choose one level 9 Warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and regain the use when you finish a Long Rest.
When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots instead of half of them.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can force it to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target takes 8d10 Psychic damage if it isn't a Fiend and has the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore it.

You have learned eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge. You gain one invocation of your choice, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table. You can replace one invocation with another one for which you qualify whenever you gain a Warlock level.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage. Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage rolls. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time.
Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock. You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness, both magical and nonmagical, within 120 feet of yourself.
You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain Concentration.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage. Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock. You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell with this feature, you don't roll the die for the Temporary Hit Points; you automatically get the highest number on the die.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock. You have received knowledge from an elder entity of the multiverse, allowing you to gain one Origin feat of your choice. Repeatable: choose a different Origin feat each time.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage via an Attack Roll. Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that requires an attack roll. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time.
Prerequisite: Level 15+ Warlock. You have Truesight with a range of 30 feet.

Choose one of the following roles. Protector: proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor. Thaumaturge: you know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list, and a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).
Protector. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.
Thaumaturge. You know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list. In addition, you gain a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. Each time you use it, choose which Channel Divinity effect to create: Divine Spark or Turn Undead. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and add them together. Each Undead that fails its save against that use takes Radiant damage equal to the total. This damage does not end the turn effect.
As a Magic action, expend a use of Channel Divinity to restore a number of Hit Points equal to five times your Cleric level, divided among Bloodied creatures within 30 feet of yourself.
When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores Hit Points to a creature, that creature regains additional Hit Points equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.
Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures other than yourself, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.
When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Life Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.
Whenever you cast a spell or use Channel Divinity to restore Hit Points with a die roll, you can forgo rolling: each die instead contributes its maximum value.
You gain one of the following options of your choice: Divine Strike or Potent Spellcasting.
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful: Divine Strike's extra damage becomes 2d8, and Potent Spellcasting can grant Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier to yourself or a creature within 60 feet.

You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. You always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared. You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages: creatures that know Druidic automatically spot such a message, and others can tell a message is present with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but cannot decipher it without magic.

Choose one of the following roles. Magician: you know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list, and a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1). Warden: proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.
Magician. You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, you gain a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).
Warden. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

Once per Long Rest, when you finish a Short Rest, recover expended spell slots with a combined level no higher than half your Druid level (round up); none of them may be level 6 or higher. Separately, you can cast one level 1+ spell you have prepared from your Circle Spells feature without expending a spell slot; you must finish a Long Rest before doing so again.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, choose one type of land: arid, polar, temperate, or tropical; you have the spells listed for your Druid level and lower prepared. The choice replaces the previous land's list rather than adding to it.
You gain one of the following options of your choice: Potent Spellcasting or Primal Strike.
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form's attack in Wild Shape, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (your choice).

The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful: Primal Strike's extra damage becomes 2d8, and Potent Spellcasting increases the range of your Druid cantrips with a range of 10 feet or more by 300 feet.

As a Bonus Action, assume a Beast form you know. You keep your HP, Hit Dice, INT/WIS/CHA, creature type and languages; your physical scores, AC (if higher), speeds, senses and attacks come from the beast. You gain Temporary HP equal to your Druid level.

Once on each of your turns, if you have no Wild Shape uses left, you can expend a spell slot to regain one use (no action). Alternatively, expend one use to gain a level 1 spell slot (no action); this direction needs a Long Rest before it can be used again.
You can cast spells while in a Beast form, except spells whose material component has a specified cost or is consumed by the spell.

Evergreen Wild Shape: when you roll Initiative and have no Wild Shape uses left, you regain one. Nature Magician: convert Wild Shape uses into a spell slot of twice that level. Longevity: for every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year (narrative; not modelled mechanically).

Magic action + one Wild Shape use: a 10-foot-radius Sphere within 60 feet. Chosen creatures make a Constitution save against your spell save DC, taking 2d6 Necrotic (3d6 at 10, 4d6 at 14) or half on a success; one creature in the area regains the same number of d6.
You are immune to the Poisoned condition and have Resistance to the damage type of your current land: arid Fire, polar Cold, temperate Lightning, tropical Poison.

Magic action + one Wild Shape use: a 15-foot Cube on the ground within 120 feet for 1 minute or until you are Incapacitated or die. You and your allies have Half Cover there, and allies also gain your Nature's Ward resistance. A Bonus Action moves it up to 60 feet.
Once per Long Rest, when you finish a Short Rest, recover expended spell slots with a combined level no higher than half your Wizard level (round up); none of them may be level 6 or higher.

You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.
Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in the chosen skill.

Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free. In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared with another level 1+ spell from the book.

When you cast a Wizard spell with a level 1-5 spell slot that deals damage, you can maximize its damage. The first use before a Long Rest costs nothing; each later use deals escalating Necrotic damage to you right after the cast, ignoring Resistance and Immunity.

Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have them prepared and can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. Each Long Rest you can study your spellbook and replace one of them with another eligible spell of the same level.

Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have them prepared and can cast each once at level 3 without expending a spell slot, regaining both uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
